answer: Here is one concrete wall: Reclaim protocol proof of account age. It works because a proof that a web2 account is years old, and the nectar it creates is a cost that scales with the size of the farm. Honest agents barely notice the check, because a proof that a web2 account is years old is something they already have; the plume falls entirely on the farm, which must buy or steal it a hundred times. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the dune for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
